matches.rationale: Ground truth describes inflated sample efficiency metrics in Figure 6(b) that are inconsistent with learning curves in Figure 6(a). Findings 3, 4, and 5 all identify inconsistencies between Figure 6(b) and Table 2 in Appendix B.6, showing reported SE_ave and SE_peak values that don't match the underlying data. These capture the same data integrity issue of inflated/inconsistent metrics.

Ground truth describes a sign error in the advantage weighting formula and ambiguity about gradient ascent alignment. Finding 2 discusses a different issue about mini-batch vs full-batch gradient descent in the TracIn equation. Finding 6 discusses reference policy circularity, not the advantage sign convention. No finding matches this specific logic error.

Ground truth identifies failure to disclose which specific p value was used for each environment in main results, with optimal p varying dramatically. Finding 3 directly identifies this issue, noting the contradiction between Section 5.2 claiming to report 'the best' p and the actual p values used versus what Table 2 shows as optimal.

Ground truth identifies overclaiming in the abstract about 'eliminating' sample inefficiency and 'completely solving' training instability, unsupported by partial improvements shown in results. Findings 7 and 8 both identify these overclaims, noting the abstract's absolute statements contradict the 20-67% improvements and lack of systematic stability evaluation.

Ground truth concerns fabricated or premature citations to 2025 works (Cheng et al., Deng et al.) that may not exist or be peer-reviewed. No finding addresses citation verification or reference fabrication issues.

Ground truth identifies missing ethical discussion in Section 7 regarding safety-critical LLM applications, failure modes, and societal impact. Finding 10 mentions limitations but focuses on technical overclaims versus acknowledged limitations, not the absence of ethical considerations. No finding matches this omission.

Ground truth identifies inappropriate marketing-style language in the introduction ('revolutionary breakthrough', 'unprecedented', 'for the first time in history'). Finding 10 directly identifies this rhetorical exaggeration in Section 1, noting hyperbolic language like 'groundbreaking contributions' and 'revolutionary breakthrough' that is undermined by acknowledged limitations.

Ground truth identifies contradiction between Section 3.1 (dynamic reference policy updated each round) and Appendix A.2 (fixed reference policy trained to convergence). Finding 6 directly captures this contradiction, noting the circular dependency and conflicting statements about 'fixed, pre-trained policy' versus 'dynamic reference evolves with training.'

Ground truth describes manipulation of y-axis ranges in Figure 6(a) to visually amplify differences (selective cropping, narrow ranges). No finding addresses visual encoding manipulation or selective axis range choices in the learning curves.

Ground truth identifies unfair comparison where IIF benefits from environment-specific hyperparameter optimization (various p values tested) while baselines use default hyperparameters without similar tuning. No finding addresses this asymmetric experimental design or baseline hyperparameter optimization.

Ground truth identifies cherry-picking favorable interpretations despite wide confidence intervals and inconsistent performance (e.g., BipedalWalker CI [24.40, 75.99], Highway round 9 degradation). Finding 9 discusses CI calculation methodology but not the interpretation issues or evidence of inconsistent improvement. Finding 12 mentions different seed counts but not the variance/cherry-picking issue.

Ground truth identifies missing learning rate η_j in the influence score formula and inconsistent use of θ_j^{(k)} notation. Finding 2 discusses TracIn equation issues but focuses on mini-batch vs full-batch, not the missing learning rate or notational inconsistency in the influence score definition.

Ground truth identifies potential selective reporting of environments, noting appendix mentions of failures (difficulty-based filtering, TD error heuristics) without disclosure of all tested environments or negative results. No finding addresses selective environment reporting or publication bias.

Ground truth identifies misattribution of the f^{return} formulation to Sutton & Barto Section 13.4, conflating standard REINFORCE with their novel construction using π^{ref}. No finding addresses this specific reference misattribution or theoretical grounding issue.

Ground truth identifies contradiction between Section 5.1 claiming 'negligible overhead' and detailed timing data showing influence calculation is 7-15% of per-round time and exceeds forward passes in LLM setting. Finding 11 discusses optimizer inconsistency (SGD vs Adam) but not computational overhead claims versus actual measurements.
